Surah 93: Al-Duha

Meccan, and its verses number eleven.

{By the morning brightness} refers to the time when the sun rises high and the day begins. They said: its singling out for an oath is because it is the hour in which Musa (peace be upon him) spoke with his Lord and in which the magicians were thrown down prostrate, according to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and that the people be gathered at mid-morning﴾. It was also said that by it is meant the day, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿that Our punishment come upon them in the morning﴾, in contrast to "bayatan" (by night).

﴿And the night﴾ i.e., the night in general.

﴿When it grows still﴾ i.e., its people fall quiet, or its darkness settles. It is derived from *sajā al-baḥr sajwan* (the sea became calm), when its waves subside.

It is related from Qatadah, Muqatil and Ja'far al-Sadiq that what is meant by the forenoon is the forenoon in which God Most High spoke to Musa (peace be upon him), and by the night, the night of the *mi'raj* (the Prophet's ascent to heaven).

And His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you﴾ is the response to the oath. That is, He has not cut you off in the manner of one who bids farewell. It is also read with the lightened form (*takhfif*, a recitation variant), meaning "He has not left you." ﴿Nor has He hated you﴾ means "nor has He detested you." The omission of the object (*hadhf al-maf'ul*) is either because it is dispensed with by its mention earlier, or because the aim is to negate the occurrence of the action from Him, exalted is He, altogether. Moreover, this respects the verse-endings (*fawasil*, the rhyming terminations of the verses). It is narrated that revelation was delayed from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for some days because he had omitted the exception (*istithna'*), as has passed in Surat al-Kahf, or in order to rebuke a persistent questioner. So the polytheists said: "Muhammad's Lord has forsaken him and hated him." Then this was revealed in refutation of them, and as good news to him, peace and blessings be upon him, of the honour that has been obtained and that is awaited. This is indicated by the mention of the name "Lord" (*al-Rabb*), which points to nurture and conveying (the message) to perfection, together with its addition to his pronoun, peace and blessings be upon him. Since what preceded includes the negation of forsaking and hatred, it implies that He, exalted is He, continues to connect him with revelation and honour in this world, so He gave him the good news, peace and blessings be upon him, that what He will bestow upon him in the Hereafter is greater and more magnificent than that. Hence it was said: *

﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first (life)﴾ because it is lasting and pure, free from all impurities absolutely, whereas this (world) is transient and mixed with harms. And the honour of prophethood bestowed upon him, peace and blessings be upon him, although it is of such a kind that no honour equals it and no excellence approaches it, (p-170)

yet he does not, in this world, remain free from some grievous accidents in the enforcement of the rulings. Moreover, what has been prepared for him, peace and blessings be upon him, in the Hereafter, of precedence and pre-eminence over all the prophets and messengers on the Day of Gathering, the Day when people stand before the Lord of the worlds; and his community being witnesses over the rest of the nations; and the raising of the ranks of the believers and the elevating of their stations through his intercession; and other sublime honours that expression cannot encompass, are, relative to the aims, like some preliminaries. It has also been said: what is meant by "the Hereafter" is the outcome of his affair, peace and blessings be upon him, that is: the end of your affair is better than its beginning; you continue to grow in strength and ascend in elevation.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be content﴾. This is a generous promise, encompassing what Allah the Exalted gave him in this world: the perfection of the soul, the knowledge of the earlier and later generations, the manifestation of his affair, the elevation of the religion through the conquests that took place in his own time (upon him be blessings and peace), in the days of his rightly-guided caliphs and others among the Islamic rulers, and the spread of the call and of Islam to the easts and wests of the earth. It also encompasses what He stored up for him of honours that no one knows except Allah the Exalted. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) reported a portion of these when the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "In Paradise there are a thousand palaces of white pearl, whose dust is musk."

The lam here is the lam of initiation (lam al-ibtida', the lam that opens a sentence and emphasizes it). It entered upon the predicate (khabar) to affirm the content of the sentence, and the subject is omitted; its estimated form is: "Verily, you, your Lord will surely give you..." It is not the lam of oath (lam al-qasam), because the lam of oath does not enter upon the imperfect verb except together with the emphatic nun (nun al-tawkid). Combining it with sawfa indicates that the giving is certain to happen, even if it is delayed for some wisdom.

It has been said that it is the lam of oath. The general rule of the necessary linkage between it and the emphatic nun has been qualified by the grammarians with two exceptions. The first is when a particle of futurity (harf al-tanfis) separates it from the verb, as in this verse and in the saying: "By Allah, I will surely give you" (la-sa-u'tika). The second is when a complement of the verb (ma'mul al-fi'l) separates them, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, to Allah you will be gathered﴾ (Q 3:158).

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: this lam is not the one in your saying "Inna Zaydan la-qa'imun" (Indeed Zayd is standing); rather it is the one in your saying "La-aqumanna" (I will surely stand), and sawfa has taken the place of one of the two emphatic nuns. It is as if it were said: "wa-la-yu'tiyannaka" (and He will surely give you). Likewise the lam in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the Hereafter is surely better for you than the first﴾ (Q 93:4), and so on.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 93, verse 6:

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge?﴾ This is an enumeration of the great kinds of blessing which God bestowed upon him, peace and blessings be upon him, from the beginning of his affair until that time, so that he would take the present and existing as evidence for the awaited and promised, whereby his heart would be reassured and his breast would be expanded. The hamzah (interrogative particle) is for the rebuke of a negation and for affirming the negated in the most emphatic manner, as if it were said: "He has indeed found you...", etc. The verb wajada (found) here means "to know" (al-'ilm), and "yatiman" (an orphan) is its second object. It has also been said that it means "to find/encounter" (al-musadaqah), and "yatiman" is a circumstantial state (hal) of its object.

It is narrated that his father died while he was still in the womb, six months having passed, and his mother died when he was eight years old. So his paternal uncle Abu Talib took him under his care, and God inclined his heart toward him, and he raised him well; and that is the meaning of "giving refuge."

It is also read "fa-awa" (with the verb from a different root), which is either from awahu, meaning "gave him refuge" (aawahu), or from awa lahu, meaning "showed him compassion" (idha rahimahu).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He found you lost﴾ is coordinated (*'atf*, grammatical coordination) with what the preceding denial (*inkar*, rhetorical rebuke) implies, as has been pointed out, or with the negated present-tense verb with *lam* (*al-mudari' al-manfi bi-lam*), which falls under its ruling. It is as if it were said: "Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter, and find you unaware of the laws (*shara'i'*) which the intellects cannot reach by themselves?" This is like His saying: ﴿You did not know what the Book was﴾. It is also said: he went astray in his childhood in some of the valleys of Makkah, and Abu Jahl returned him to 'Abd al-Muttalib. It is also said: he went astray another time, and they searched for him but did not find him. So 'Abd al-Muttalib circled the Ka'bah seven times and humbly supplicated God Exalted. Then they heard a caller calling from the sky: "O assembly of people, do not clamor, for Muhammad has a Lord who will not forsake him or lose him, and Muhammad is in the valley of Tihamah near the *sumr* tree." So 'Abd al-Muttalib and Waraqah ibn Nawfal set out, and behold, the Prophet (ﷺ) was standing under a tree, playing with its branches and leaves. It is also said: his wet-nurse Halimah lost him at the gate of Makkah when she weaned him, and she came with him to return him to 'Abd al-Muttalib. It is also said: he went astray on the road to Syria when Abu Talib took him out.

It is narrated that Iblis seized the reins of his she-camel on a dark night and diverted him from the road. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) came and blew a blast on Iblis, from which he fell to the land of India, and he returned the Prophet (ﷺ) to the caravan.

﴿And He guided you﴾: He guided you to the paths (*manahij*) of the laws (*shara'i'*) contained within what was revealed to you of the Clear Book, and taught you what you did not know. Or it means He removed your error concerning your grandfather or your uncle.

**Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 93, verse 8:**

﴿And He found you poor﴾, i.e., in need. It is also read as "ʿayyilan" (burdened with dependents), and it is read as "ʿadiman" (one who has nothing).

﴿Then He enriched you﴾: He enriched you with the wealth of Khadijah, or with wealth that came to you from the profit of trade, or with wealth that accrued to you from the spoils of war. The Prophet ﷺ said: "My provision has been placed under the shade of my spear." And it has been said: He made you content and enriched your heart.

﴿So as for the orphan, do not oppress him﴾: do not overpower him concerning his property. Mujahid said: do not belittle him. It is also recited as "فَلا تَكْهَرْ" (fa-lā takhar, a recitation variant, qirā'a), meaning: do not frown in his face.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 93, verse 10:

﴿As for the one who asks, do not repel him.﴾ That is: do not rebuke him, nor speak harshly to him; rather, turn him away with gentle words (radd jamil). Ibrahim ibn Adham said: "How excellent a saying is 'the beggar': they carry our provision to the Hereafter." Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "The beggar, who seeks the Hereafter, comes to the door of one of you and says: 'Will you send something to your family?'" It has also been said: what is meant here by "the one who asks" is the one who asks about the religion.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 93, verse 11:

﴿And as for the favour of your Lord, speak of it﴾ by giving thanks for it, spreading it, and making its effects and its rulings known. By "it" is meant what Allah Most High bestowed upon him, peace be upon him, of the various kinds of blessings, among which are the blessings that are counted, those already present and those promised. The meaning is: you were an orphan, lost, and poor, and Allah Most High sheltered you, guided you, and enriched you. So whatever may be the case, do not forget the rights of Allah Most High's blessing upon you in these three matters. Follow the example of Allah Most High and be good as Allah has been good to you. So show tenderness to the orphan and shelter him, have mercy on the one who asks, look after him with your kindness, and do not turn him away from your door. Speak of all the blessings of Allah. Since the greatest of them is the blessing of prophethood, the command includes his guidance of those who had gone astray, and his teaching of the laws and rulings according to what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, guided him to and taught him of the Book and the Wisdom.

From the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surah al-Duha, Allah Most High will count him among those with whom Muhammad is pleased to intercede for him, and Allah will record for him ten good deeds for every orphan and every one who asks."
